## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `cloudron migrate source build install to community app catalog versions-url` → 0 hits

- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:117-128` ("Catalog Updates Versus Source Rebuilds"); `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58` (lists `--versions-url` for install/update)
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — docs only; facts below are verified
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** After publishing a new Cloudron community package, the operator asked for "the process for changing apps from our build to community app linked". It had been done once (a package's notes record a fresh `cloudron install --versions-url` on 2026-10-16, then uninstalling the source-built test app) but never captured in aidevops guidance, so the session couldn't find it.

## What

Add a short subsection after "Catalog Updates Versus Source Rebuilds" in `cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md`: **Moving a source-built install to the catalog**.

Verified facts to state (Cloudron CLI 8.2.6, `src/actions.js`):

- Only `cloudron install --versions-url <url>[@version]` links an app to a catalog. It calls `/api/v1/community/app` and sends `versionsUrl` with the install (`actions.js:540-548, 667-668`).
- `cloudron update` has no `--versions-url` option. It can switch an app to the catalog's digest-pinned image (the scratch-manifest method already documented at lines 124-128) but doesn't make the app catalog-linked, so it never receives catalog updates.
- So the switch is: back up → install a new copy from the catalog → move data or users → verify → uninstall the source-built app.

Procedure to document:

1. `cloudron backup create --app <old>`.
2. If data matters: `cloudron export --app <old>` and later `cloudron import --app <new> ...` (verify flags with `cloudron export --help` / `cloudron import --help` at implementation time), or restore through the dashboard's Import. If it was only a test instance, start fresh.
3. `cloudron install --versions-url <catalog-url> --location <temp-or-final-location>`. A location can hold only one app, so either install at a temporary location and use `cloudron set-location` after uninstalling the old app, or uninstall first (destructive, so confirm).
4. Verify health, sign-in and stored credentials, then `cloudron uninstall --app <old>`.
5. Confirm the new app reports catalog updates (dashboard shows the community source; `cloudron status --app <new>` shows the catalog image digest).

Also correct `cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58`, which lists `--versions-url` as an `update` flag. In CLI 8.2.6 it's install-only.

## Why

Without this, every new package's production test install stays on a source build and silently misses updates, or an agent has to rediscover the CLI behaviour.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Docs-only change of about 20 lines with verified facts supplied.

### Implementation Steps

1. Run `cloudron export --help` and `cloudron import --help` (CLI 8.2.6) and use the exact flags.
2. Write the subsection; keep it under about 25 lines.
3. Fix the server-ops flag line; run the linters.

title: docs(cloudron): use update --versions-url to switch a source-built app to its catalog
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `cloudron update versions-url catalog switch` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: corrects guidance merged for #35003 (`e216d12840`)
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:135-151`, `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58`
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple`; implemented interactively
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** #35003's brief was written against Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 and said `cloudron update` cannot link an app to a catalog. When the documented install-and-import route was used on a real Cloudron 10.1.5 server, `cloudron import` failed. The in-place switch below then worked.

## What

Verified on Cloudron 10.1.5 (`GET /api/v1/cloudron/status`) with CLI 9.0.3:

- CLI 9.0.0+ has `cloudron update --app <app> --versions-url <url>[@version] --force`. Its changelog says it updates or switches a community app's `CloudronVersions.json` URL; `--force` is required for a source-type change. It POSTs `{versionsUrl, skipBackup, force}` to `/api/v1/apps/<id>/update`, keeps the app ID, data, Postgres database, location and mailbox, and backs up first unless `--no-backup` is passed.
- Result: `cloudron status` shows `Source: <catalog URL>` and the catalog's digest-pinned image. The old `local/...` image is deleted, and `/app/data` secrets are untouched.
- `cloudron import --remote-path ... --backup-format tgz` fails against Cloudron 10 with `400 format must be string`: CLI 8.2.6 and 9.0.3 both send `backupFormat`. So the install-new-copy-and-import route in the current text doesn't work from the CLI.
- CLI 8.x has no `update --versions-url`. Check `cloudron --version` first; `npx -y cloudron@9 ...` runs the newer CLI without changing the global install and uses the same `~/.cloudron.json`.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:135-151`: make the in-place `update --versions-url --force` the primary procedure (check CLI version, optional manual backup, run, verify `Source:`/digest/health/secrets). Keep the reinstall route only as a fallback, noting that CLI import is broken on Cloudron 10.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-server-ops-skill.md:58`: `--versions-url` works with `install` and, on CLI 9.0+, with `update` (with `--force` to switch source).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The publishing skill documents `cloudron update --versions-url <url> --force` (CLI 9.0+) as the switch route and states the Cloudron 10 import failure.
- [ ] The server-ops skill no longer says `--versions-url` is install-only.
- [ ] `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` passes.

**Task ID:** `t18721` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

feat(badges): worktree-safe badges sync --apply and scheduled drift remediation

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Keep managed README badge blocks current automatically. Today a template fix
(e.g. GH#34145, GH#35012) only reaches a repo when someone runs
`aidevops init` or `aidevops badges sync --apply` by hand, so ~50 managed repos
kept an outdated badge block (language chart inline with badges) for weeks.

Two gaps:

1. `badges-sync-helper.sh --apply` mutates canonical checkouts:
   `git pull --ff-only` then `git checkout -q -B <branch>` in the canonical
   repo path, commit, push, then checkout back. This violates the
   linked-worktree invariant (interactive and automated sessions never switch
   or create branches in a canonical checkout) and skips any repo whose
   canonical checkout is dirty or off its default branch.
2. No routine runs drift detection + remediation. `badges-check-helper.sh`
   is only run manually.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`: create a linked worktree per repo
  from `origin/<default-branch>` (via `worktree-helper.sh add`), run
  `readme-badges-helper.sh inject` + `repo-metrics-helper.sh generate` +
  `check` inside it, commit, push, open the PR with `gh_create_pr`, then
  release the worktree. Never touch the canonical checkout.
- Add a weekly routine (pulse/maintenance path that already iterates
  maintained repos, see `test-maintenance-repo-selection.sh` for the repo
  selector) that runs `badges-check-helper.sh --json` and opens one sync PR per
  DRIFTED owned-org repo, deduplicating against an open sync PR.
- Respect owned-org scope (`badge-orgs.conf`), STARTER-OWNED, local-only and
  contributed repos exactly as today.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/badges-check-helper.sh`
- `.agents/aidevops/badges.md`

## What

Add a recommended repository protection baseline for Cloudron package repos to the publishing guidance, and show how to apply it.

## Why

`.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:199` says "Review protection, Actions permissions, package checks and credentials before enabling the variable" but gives no baseline. A package repo was published with no protection at all. The guide says published versions are append-only, yet nothing stopped a `v*` tag from being moved or deleted, or `main` from being force-pushed. On 2026-10-18 the owner applied two rulesets to seven package repos. Neither conflicts with the catalog workflow, which only fast-forwards `main` and creates new tags (`git push --atomic origin HEAD:main "v${VERSION}"`), nor with the metrics and Star History callers, which only fast-forward `main` (the metrics helper force-pushes only its own PR branch).

Applied baseline, both `enforcement: active` with no bypass actors:

1. Branch ruleset, `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`: `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`.
2. Tag ruleset, `refs/tags/v*`: `update`, `deletion`. Creation stays allowed because the publish job creates the tag with the job token.

Full PR gating (require pull request plus required checks) is a separate, optional step. It blocks the workflows' direct pushes to `main` unless the owner is a bypass actor and the pushes use owner PATs (`CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT`, `SYNC_PAT`). That bypass path is not yet verified with fine-grained PATs, so do not recommend it without testing.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md:191-200`. After the publication-enable paragraph, add a short "Repository protection" paragraph with the two rulesets above, why each is compatible with the catalog workflow, and that PR gating needs bypass and PATs.

It must refuse to create a duplicate when a ruleset with the same name exists, and must require an explicit flag to apply, because `.agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md:158` says protection changes are a deliberate maintainer action. If adding the subcommand is not clean, keep this to documentation.

Reference: `marcusquinn/aidevops` itself has the tag ruleset "Protect aidevops release tags" (`refs/tags/v*`; creation, update, deletion; owner bypass). Package repos must not block tag creation, because the workflow, not the owner, creates their tags.

## Task


Stop the assign/unassign loop between two normalization passes. It holds an
`origin:interactive` issue left at `status:in-progress` with no live worker and
no interactive stamp. The issue is never dispatched again, and its draft-PR
checkpoint is never resumed.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the assign/unassign loop between two normalization passes. It holds an
`origin:interactive` issue left at `status:in-progress` with no live worker and
no interactive stamp. The issue is never dispatched again, and its draft-PR
checkpoint is never resumed.

## Why (observed 2026-10-18, v3.39.43, three runners on one managed private repo)

- One issue (`origin:interactive`, `auto-dispatch`, `status:in-progress`) has
  had 28 assign/unassign events across three runners since 2026-10-11, about
  one per hour. There has been no DISPATCH_CLAIM or worker activity since the
  original worker's launch, and its draft PR has been idle for 7 days.
- Pass 1, `_normalize_reassign_self`
  (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`, about lines 675-726), assigns
  every `status:queued`/`status:in-progress` issue that has zero assignees to
  whichever runner is normalizing. It writes no claim stamp.
- Pass 2, `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` (same file, about lines
  807-894), lists that runner's `origin:interactive` assignments older than the
  threshold with no stamp. For any status other than `status:in-review` it
  removes only the assignee (`gh issue edit --remove-assignee`) and leaves
  `status:in-progress` in place.
- On the next cycle, Pass 1 on any runner matches again. Log evidence:
  `Stampless interactive auto-release: unassigned <runner> from #N ... (>3600s old, no stamp)`.
  Between releases, dedup logs
  `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: issue #N ... is assigned` and
  `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim_unverified signal=ASSIGNED`.
- Knock-on effect: the wedged issue is also the footprint-overlap blocker for
  another available issue. That issue roots a 6-issue dependency chain.

## How (recommended; the worker may refine with evidence)

1. In `_normalize_reassign_self`, do not fabricate ownership. Skip issues where
   the stampless pass would immediately release this runner:
   `origin:interactive` issues with no interactive stamp for `runner_user`.
   More generally, skip issues with no live dispatch claim/lease for this
   runner.
2. In `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive`, when releasing a stampless
   `status:in-progress`/`status:queued` claim, also reset the lifecycle state
   with `set_issue_status ... "available" --remove-assignee`, as the
   `status:in-review` branch already does. Then dispatch dedup / the
   draft-checkpoint continuation path owns the next step instead of the
   reassign pass.
3. Keep the t1996 multi-runner guard and every existing trust and stamp check.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`

## Task


When a launched worker reports `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`,
that runner should stop reclaiming the same unchanged task. A capable runner
should still be able to claim it. Today the same incapable runner relaunches
the task repeatedly. After that, a non-canonical reason string strands the
issue at `status:blocked`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a launched worker reports `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`,
that runner should stop reclaiming the same unchanged task. A capable runner
should still be able to claim it. Today the same incapable runner relaunches
the task repeatedly. After that, a non-canonical reason string strands the
issue at `status:blocked`.

## Why (observed 2026-10-18, v3.39.41-v3.39.43, managed private repo)

- One code-fix issue received 8 `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` comments from
  the same runner in 62 minutes (03:17-04:19Z). Each one carried
  `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet ... Projected state: status:available`
  with the same `terminal-blocker-observation revision=... blocker=...`
  fingerprint. Each was a full worker launch.
- The runner-local cooldown in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
  (GH#33743, about lines 1018-1221) is recorded only from the pre-dispatch
  signal
  `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=runner_capability_unmet signal=... cooldown=eligible`
  (`runner-capability-helper.sh`). A capability gap discovered by the worker
  after launch never feeds that cooldown.
- `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` deliberately excludes `runner_capability_unmet`
  from circuit/backoff evidence (about lines 593 and 625), so nothing throttles
  this runner.
- A second runner then ended with the non-canonical line
  `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=verification_environment_missing_prerequisites`.
  The blocker was missing native host binaries needed by a repository test.
  The worker contract in `headless-runtime-lib.sh` (about lines 1066-1079)
  classes this as `runner_capability_unmet`. It was recorded as `unknown`
  with projected `status:blocked`, so no runner retries it.
- Impact: this one issue is the root of an 89-issue dependency chain. A
  different runner platform skips the failing host-specific test and could
  complete the task.

## How (recommended)

1. Record the existing runner-local capability cooldown from a trusted
   terminal-blocker observation. Conditions: the latest observation is
   `runner_capability_unmet`, it was posted by this runner's own login, and
   its task revision is unchanged. Keying and TTL match the pre-dispatch
   cooldown. Other runners stay eligible, and no global label is applied.
2. Normalize unrecognized `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON` values that describe a
   missing local tool or environment prerequisite to
   `runner_capability_unmet`. Do this only if the existing classifier has an
   allowlist hook for aliases; otherwise record the gap in the PR and keep
   scope to step 1.
3. Preserve all trust-boundary checks (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).

# Qualify provider-only inference containment using the existing worker egress contract

**Status:** Held capability/design brief, prepared on 2026-10-18. The operator
approved preparing this brief only. Implementation, worker dispatch, backend
configuration, infrastructure provisioning and model/comparison execution are not
authorized. Keep this work separate from application enrichment policy.

## Goal and observed gap

Provide a reviewed, verifiable route for source-extraction inference that can
contact its selected model provider while remaining unable to retrieve external
source pages, reach private services, read evaluator material or escape its
per-invocation filesystem boundary.

An offline construction component has passed a real Linux deny-all-network jail
check. That proves construction isolation, not online inference containment. The
current session has `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_EGRESS_BACKEND` unset or empty. A tool-denied
runtime profile is not evidence of kernel/process-tree isolation, and fake-backend
fixtures are not deployable enforcing backends.

This is an observed qualification/configuration gap in this environment, not a
claim that the framework has no implementation anywhere.

## Deduplication and evidence

- Memory recall for provider-only inference containment returned no relevant
  lessons.

title: UI guidance: forms default to field names as placeholders (unless specified), lighter than typed text
body:
## What

Add a default form rule to the framework's UI guidance: **typed form fields show the field's name as their placeholder, unless the project's DESIGN.md or the task specifies otherwise.** Pair it with the colour rule that makes this safe: a placeholder is visibly lighter than typed text and still meets 4.5:1 against the field.

Rule text to add (adapt wording to each file's style):

- Text, email, phone, message (textarea) and each part of a name field use the field's name as placeholder text by default. Keep the visible label above the field: the placeholder never replaces it. Leave "(optional)" and required markers out of the placeholder ("Approximate budget", not "Approximate budget (optional)").
- Use a format hint instead of the name where it helps more ("https://" for a URL, "Search services" for a searchable multi-select, an example date format). Selects keep their own empty-choice text.
- Placeholder colour: lighter than typed text so an empty field never looks filled in, and at least 4.5:1 against the field background in light and dark modes. A palette-relative pattern that works for both: the input's text colour mixed about 75% towards the field background (`color-mix(in srgb, <text> 75%, <field>)`), with the plain text colour as the fallback for browsers without `color-mix()`. Never give placeholders the typed text's own colour, and do not start from a decorative/muted token that already fails 4.5:1.
- Record the project's choice (default, or an exception) in DESIGN.md's components/forms section.

## Why

Owner preference across projects, stated during a site design pass (2026-10-18): forms should show field names as placeholder text where relevant unless specified. Without a framework default, each project's agents leave placeholders empty or invent per-form text, and the preference has to be restated per project.

Observed pitfall when applying it: a theme-integration rule gave placeholders the input's own text colour, so every empty field looked filled in. Measured on Kadence palettes: typed text 11.99:1 (light) / 15.62:1 (dark) and placeholder identical; after mixing the text 75% towards the field, the placeholder was 5.52:1 light and 9.31:1 dark (Chromium and WebKit agree). Public fix and evidence: wpallstars/seoprostack#844 (PR #846). Kadence's default palette 6 placeholder alone is 4.02:1 on white, below WCAG AA.

## How / Files

- `.agents/product/ui-design.md` — add a short "Forms" subsection under "Design System Foundation" (after "Typography" or "Spacing and Layout") with the rule above; add one Accessibility Checklist item: "Placeholders are lighter than typed text and at least 4.5:1; labels stay visible."
- `.agents/tools/design/design-md.md` — in "Creating a DESIGN.md" (the `buttons_and_forms` → §7 Components mapping, around line 258) note that §7 records the form placeholder policy (field names by default, exceptions) and the placeholder colour token/derivation; in "Evolving an existing DESIGN.md during UI work" (around line 82) nothing new is needed unless wording conflicts.
- Optional, only if it shows inputs without placeholders: `.agents/tools/design/library/_template/preview.html.template` (Components section near line 599) so the preview input example shows a placeholder beside a typed value.

- `tools/design/design-md.md` tells agents to record the placeholder policy and colour in DESIGN.md §7.
- No contradiction with existing accessibility guidance (labels remain required; placeholder is never the only label).

## Verification

- The repository's agent-doc checks (progressive-disclosure / size ratchet) pass unchanged.

## What

A planning publication silently reverted TODO.md lines that were already on its base commit. t18504 (GH#32714, PR #33047) added a 3-way merge to stop this, but it happened again on 2026-10-18.

## Evidence

- `44e2863135` (planning publication, 15:04Z) marked `t18720` done (`pr:#35021 completed:2026-10-18`) and added `t18723` (GH#35032).
- PR #35048 (`planning/a06775cbc835-plan-add-t18727-t18728-pre-existing-test-failure`, author marcusquinn, labels `origin:interactive`, `allow-auto-merge`) has a single commit `b92c85d528`, whose parent is `a855452528` (15:23Z).
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 44e2863135 a855452528` → ancestor. So the base already contained both lines.
- `git show b92c85d528 -- TODO.md` nevertheless shows:
  - `t18720` reverted from `[x] ... pr:#35021 completed:2026-10-18` to `[ ]`
  - `t18723` line deleted
  - `t18727`, `t18728` added (the intended change)
- PR file stats: `TODO.md +5 -2`. The `-2` are the clobbered lines.

So the publisher produced TODO.md from a stale copy (likely the canonical checkout's TODO.md, which predated `44e2863135`) and committed it as a whole-file replacement on a fresher base, rather than 3-way merging the intended delta.

Repaired by hand in PR #35061 (restores both lines).

## How

1. Find the code path that built #35048's commit: `planning-commit-helper.sh` and the planning publisher used by `claim-task-id.sh` / TODO add flows (branch prefix `planning/<hash>-plan-...`, trailer `Planning-Publication-ID`).
2. Confirm where the TODO.md content comes from (canonical working copy vs. `origin/main` blob) and whether the t18504 3-way merge (`base` = blob the edit was made against, `ours` = edited file, `theirs` = current `origin/main`) runs on this path. The likely gap: the merge base is taken as the publication base instead of the version the edit was made from, which turns a stale snapshot into a revert.
3. Fix so that only the intended delta lands; refuse to publish if the result removes or un-completes task lines not named in the publication.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`

title: release-lane-helper: report GitHub rate-limit 403 as quota exhaustion, not 'Cannot verify repository release lane'
body:
## Observed

`aidevops release reconcile <source-PR>` failed with:

```
RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=lane-head status=403 retryable=false
Cannot verify repository release lane
```

At the same moment `gh api rate_limit` reported `core.remaining: 0`, the gh-cooldown guard printed `primary-core active=true retry_at=<epoch>`, and `gh auth status` misreported the keyring token as invalid. After the reset, the same command succeeded unchanged: it queued publication and then published v3.39.45. Nothing was wrong with auth or the lane. The diagnostic pointed the operator at repository access instead of quota.

## Cause

`_release_lane_remote_head` in `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh` (around lines 108-137) maps every non-404, non-5xx status to `retryable=false` and a fatal "Cannot verify" message. GitHub returns 403 (or 429) for primary and secondary rate limits, so quota exhaustion looks identical to a permission failure. `_release_lane_api` (around lines 89-106) has the same classification.

## Proposed fix

- Before emitting the fatal message for 403/429, check whether the failure is a rate limit: the gh-cooldown state is active, the response says "rate limit", or `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`. If it is, print a distinct line such as `RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=lane-head status=403 rate_limited=true retry_after=<epoch>`, followed by "GitHub API quota exhausted; rerun after <time>". Exit with a distinct code so callers and agents do not treat it as an auth or lane fault.
- Do not add automatic retry loops. Fail closed, but with the correct cause, consistent with the comment-storm and rate-limit invariants.
- Keep never forwarding response bodies, as today.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`: `_release_lane_remote_head` and `_release_lane_api`.
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` around line 631, where "Cannot verify repository release lane" is printed for the reconcile path.
- Reference pattern: the existing gh-cooldown detection used by the shared gh wrappers (`shared-gh-wrappers*.sh`).

## Verification

- With a stubbed `gh` that returns a 403 rate-limit response (or an active cooldown marker), reconcile prints the rate-limited diagnostic and the new exit code, not "Cannot verify repository release lane".
- A genuine 403 permission failure still prints the existing fatal message with `retryable=false`.
- Run ShellCheck on the changed scripts.

2. Legacy migration preserves unique ignored/untracked contents, staged state, relevant Git administrative/history dependencies and supported filesystem metadata. Incomplete buckets remain explicitly incomplete.

title: Sensitive temp root keeps run state for months: sidecars, auth copies and session DBs outlive the 7-hour limit
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

The sensitive temp root (`~/.aidevops-private/tmp`, or `AIDEVOPS_SENSITIVE_TEMP_DIR`) stays bounded, as `sensitive-temp-helper.sh` promises. A headless run's sidecar files are removed with their base temp file. A periodic sweep removes the `aidevops-*` entries that outlive the retention window, whatever left them. On macOS the root is excluded from Time Machine, so backups do not keep what the sweep removes.

## Why

`sensitive-temp-helper.sh` creates "private framework-owned temporary directories" with cleanup guardians that "enforce a bounded maximum lifetime" (`.agents/scripts/sensitive-temp-helper.sh:5-9`). A guarded path is removed when its owner exits or after `HEADLESS_RUNTIME_TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`, 25200 s (7 h) by default (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh:106-114`), even while its owner still runs (`sensitive-temp-helper.sh:290-300`).

On one macOS runner on 2026-10-18, the root held run state from late July onwards:

- 5,215 top-level files, 4,846 of them older than 7 days. They include 4,961 `*.wait_status` and 93 `*.kill_reason` sidecars, and 153 `aidevops-headless-runtime.XXXXXX` base files older than a day. Twenty base files are over 300 KB and the largest is about 4.3 MB. Of the per-attempt files (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:223-273`), only the run output grows that large.
- 50 directories, 48 of them older than 7 days: 15 `aidevops-headless-prompt.*` (seed prompts) and 35 `aidevops-headless-auth.*` (isolated OpenCode data). Five auth directories still hold `auth.json` (mode 600, dated 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-02), `opencode.db` with its WAL, `opencode.log`, tool-output files and snapshot packs.
- `tmutil isexcluded ~/.aidevops-private` prints `[Included]`, and the runner has Time Machine destinations, so its backups hold copies too.

The root is mode 700, so other users cannot read it. Still, credential copies and worker transcripts are kept for months, not hours, and in backups. This was checked from names, sizes, modes and dates only; no file was opened.

Causes, all on `main` at 5c6ce2c:

1. **Sidecars are never registered for cleanup.** `headless-runtime-attempt.sh:253` and `:261` create each attempt's `exit_code_file` in the root and register it for EXIT-trap cleanup. Sidecars are then written next to it: `.wait_status` (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:275`), `.kill_reason` (`headless-runtime-lib.sh:1403`, `:1410`; `worker-activity-watchdog.sh:538`), `.watchdog_killed` (`worker-activity-watchdog.sh:537`), `.watchdog_stall_killed` (`worker-activity-watchdog.sh:550`) and `.rate_limit_fast` (`headless-runtime-worker.sh:284`). `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` (`headless-runtime-launch.sh:134-164`) removes only registered paths. Some readers delete the sidecar they read: `.watchdog_stall_killed` (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:353-357`, `:384-388`, `:424-428`), `.watchdog_killed` (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:688-690`) and the last attempt's `.rate_limit_fast` (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:447`). Nothing deletes `.kill_reason`. Only the EXIT trap deletes `.wait_status`, and only for the one path `_hrff_durable_exit_code_file` returns (`headless-runtime-failure.sh:1729`, `:1741`). The normal finish, `_hrw_finish_cleanup` (`headless-runtime-worker.sh:2549-2564`, called at `:2676`), clears that trap after its cleanup, so after a normal finish nothing deletes `.wait_status`. Each attempt also deletes its own base `exit_code_file` once read (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:359`, `:390`, `:429`), and every retry or fallback makes a new one (`:253`, `:373`, `:408`). The runner matches this: a later count the same day found only 2 each of `.watchdog_killed` and `.watchdog_stall_killed`, against thousands of `.wait_status` files.
2. **Most per-attempt files have no guardian.** `exit_code_file` (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:261`, `:377`, `:412`) and, for non-ephemeral roles, `output_file` (`headless-runtime-launch.sh:123-132`) are registered with `_register_headless_runtime_temp_path` only. If the worker is killed by SIGKILL, or the runner reboots, before its EXIT trap runs, they stay.
3. **Nothing sweeps the root when a guardian dies.** Guardians are detached Python processes that each watch one path (`sensitive-temp-helper.sh:215-306`). A reboot ends them. A failed `rmtree` retries for at most `max(60, poll * 5)` seconds and then gives up (`:273-279`, `:299-300`). The 50 directories, which had guardians, show that this happens.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The retention rule, sweep bounds, call site, test locations and the files to change are all decided, and no file in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf` is in the write surface. The worker still writes a delete routine with focused coverage and confirms cleanup ordering at each existing call site, so the contract is not exact enough for `tier:simple`.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `sensitive temp aidevops-private wait_status sidecar cleanup leak headless runtime guardian` → 0 hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no recent commits, related PRs or claimed issues for the target files. Searches for `wait_status`, `aidevops-private`, `sensitive temp` and `sensitive-temp-helper` found only closed, different issues: #28796 and #28800 (Linux sensitive-temp preflight) and #34556 (detached launcher logs in `/tmp`).
- [x] File refs verified: every path and line below was checked against `main` at 5c6ce2c on 2026-10-18.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. The sweep deletes files, which rules out `tier:simple`. Its bounds, name rule and symlink rule are decided below. `headless-runtime-helper.sh`, `headless-runtime-lib.sh` and `worker-activity-watchdog.sh` are in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf` and are outside the write surface.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped. The sweep and its tests are the work, so there is nothing useful to seed.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Session:** OpenCode, interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive, for the maintainer
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** A headless worker's permission hold was being diagnosed, and a listing of the sensitive temp root showed run state going back to late July. This issue names no repository, host or credential.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
sed -n '101,164p' .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh     # guardian start, registration, _cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths
sed -n '128,319p' .agents/scripts/sensitive-temp-helper.sh       # root, create_dir, guardian, cleanup
sed -n '57,101p' .agents/scripts/pulse-temp-helper.sh            # aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup: the age-sweep and source-a-helper pattern to follow
sed -n '219,283p' .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh    # per-attempt files and how each is registered
sed -n '1695,1742p' .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh  # the EXIT trap reads .wait_status before cleanup
rg -n -o '(exit_code_file|EXIT_CODE_FILE|_durable_exit_code_file)\}\.[a-z_]+' .agents/scripts --glob '!tests/**'   # every sidecar suffix
rg -n '_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths' .agents/scripts --glob '!tests/**'   # every cleanup call site
# Gotchas:
# - Sidecars are read after the worker exits: the EXIT trap reads .wait_status
#   (headless-runtime-failure.sh:1729-1741) and classify_worker_kill_reason() reads the others
#   before cleanup runs (headless-runtime-failure.sh:1677-1678). Removing them any earlier brings back
#   GH#21707 (a SIGTERM'd worker reported as reason=clean).
# - Never follow a symlink and never leave the root: keep the guardian's own rules
#   (sensitive-temp-helper.sh:225-227 and :249-250).
# - Bash 3.2: no mapfile and no associative arrays (reference/bash-compat.md).
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh:134-164`: `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` also removes each registered path's sidecars (step 1).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/sensitive-temp-helper.sh`: new `aidevops_sensitive_temp_sweep_stale` after `aidevops_sensitive_temp_cleanup` (`:308-318`), with the macOS backup exclusion (steps 2 and 4).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-temp-helper.sh:57-101`: `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` runs the sweep (step 3).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-sensitive-temp-helper.sh`: focused sweep cases (step 5).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh`: assert sidecar removal in an existing `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` case (step 5).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh`: unset `AIDEVOPS_SENSITIVE_TEMP_DIR` in its setup, next to the existing `unset AIDEVOPS_PULSE_TMP_DIR` (step 3).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` has four call sites (see the Quick-Start `rg`): the EXIT trap path (`headless-runtime-failure.sh:1677-1678`), `headless-runtime-worker.sh:2558-2559`, `headless-runtime-helper.sh:316-317` and `headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh:245-246`. Sidecar readers are the EXIT trap (`headless-runtime-failure.sh:1729-1741`), `classify_worker_kill_reason()` (`headless-runtime-failure.sh:1159`), the attempt finishers (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:350-358`, `:382-389`, `:422-428` and `:447`) and `headless-runtime-helper.sh:688-690` and `:798`. `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` is called on every pulse worker launch (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:262`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** The sidecar writers above are unchanged. The new deletions are limited to (a) the fixed sidecar suffixes of a path the run registered itself, and (b) top-level `aidevops-*` entries in the sensitive root that are past the sweep age, plus one Time Machine exclusion attribute on the root.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-sensitive-temp-helper.sh` (root, create_dir, guardian, cleanup), `test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh` (`aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup`), `test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh` (cleanup function), `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`, and `test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh` (sidecar classification).
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no new setting or environment variable is added. The sweep age is derived from the existing `HEADLESS_RUNTIME_TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`. Nothing else is generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no data migrates. On each runner, the first sweep after deployment removes the stale entries that have already built up. This is the intended clean-up.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Reverting brings back the current behaviour. Entries removed in the meantime are temp state the design already expires after 7 h. Remove the Time Machine exclusion with `tmutil removeexclusion ~/.aidevops-private/tmp`.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Sidecars go with their base path.** In `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths`, after a registered path matches one of the existing `case` patterns, also run `rm -f --` on `${path}.wait_status`, `${path}.kill_reason`, `${path}.watchdog_killed`, `${path}.watchdog_stall_killed` and `${path}.rate_limit_fast`. Use one explicit suffix list, in a single variable or loop, not a `${path}.*` glob. A sidecar that cannot be removed is a cleanup failure, recorded the same way a retained path is. Paths outside the patterns stay refused, as now. The base `exit_code_file` is usually gone by then (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:359`), so remove the sidecars whether or not the base path still exists.
2. **Sweep.** Add `aidevops_sensitive_temp_sweep_stale` to `sensitive-temp-helper.sh`, following the `python3` heredoc pattern in `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` (`pulse-temp-helper.sh:57-89`):
   - Resolve the root with `aidevops_sensitive_temp_root`. If that fails, return 0 and change nothing.
   - The age limit is `max(86400, 2 * HEADLESS_RUNTIME_TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS)` seconds, with the same 25200 default and a numeric guard.
   - Look only at top-level entries whose names start with `aidevops-`. Skip symlinks entirely: do not remove them and do not follow them.
   - A file is stale when its `lstat` mtime is older than the limit. A directory is stale when its own mtime and every mtime under it (`os.walk(..., followlinks=False)`, using `lstat`) are older than the limit, so a directory still being written is kept.
   - Remove stale files with `os.unlink` and stale directories with `shutil.rmtree`. Ignore `FileNotFoundError`, which happens when a guardian removes the entry first, and treat other `OSError`s as best-effort. Never print file contents, and never print names to stdout.
   - Return 0 when `python3` is missing.
3. **Run it from the pulse cleanup.** At the end of `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup`, source `sensitive-temp-helper.sh` from the same directory and call `aidevops_sensitive_temp_sweep_stale >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`. Do this exactly as the function already sources `pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh` (`pulse-temp-helper.sh:91-99`). In `test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh`, add `unset AIDEVOPS_SENSITIVE_TEMP_DIR` to the setup that sets `HOME` and unsets `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_TMP_DIR`, so a developer's environment cannot point the test at a real root.
4. **Keep it out of backups on macOS.** In `aidevops_sensitive_temp_sweep_stale`, when `uname -s` is `Darwin` and `tmutil` exists, run `tmutil isexcluded "$root"`. If its output starts with `[Included]`, run `tmutil addexclusion "$root"`. This is a sticky exclusion: it needs no sudo and follows the folder. It is best-effort, never fails the sweep, and is skipped elsewhere. It excludes the temp root only, not its parent.
5. **Focused coverage, in the existing files only.** In `test-sensitive-temp-helper.sh`, which already isolates `AIDEVOPS_SENSITIVE_TEMP_DIR` under its own temp folder: age entries with `touch -t 202601010000`, then assert that a stale `aidevops-` file and a stale `aidevops-` directory are removed, while a fresh file, a stale non-`aidevops-` file and a stale directory holding one fresh file are kept. Also assert that a stale `aidevops-` symlink to a folder outside the root is kept and its target untouched. In `test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh`, extend one existing `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` case to create two sidecars of a registered path and assert both are gone. Destructive code in a sensitive folder is the reason for this coverage. Add no new harness, runner or CI job.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** The sweep runs while workers run. It removes only entries older than at least 24 h, three times the guardian limit that already expires guarded paths. A race with a guardian or an EXIT trap leaves the entry gone either way.
- **Ordering:** Checked on 5c6ce2c: no call site reads a sidecar after `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` returns. `_private_workload_exit_trap` (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:312-329`), `_hrw_finish_cleanup` (`headless-runtime-worker.sh:2549-2564`) and `_hrw_cleanup_non_worker_run` (`headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh:240-252`) only release locks and leases after it. The EXIT trap reads `.wait_status` first (`headless-runtime-failure.sh:1727-1742`) and settles the exit reason before `_hrff_finalize_exit_trap` (called at `:1802`) runs the cleanup (`:1677-1678`). Check again in case the code has moved since. `test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh` and the contract tests must stay green. If a site now reads a sidecar after cleanup, move the read before it, unless that site is in a file listed in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`. In that case, leave the file alone and take the Safety-Stop route.
- **Migration/rollback:** No data migrates. The first sweep on each runner removes old entries, including old credential copies. Existing Time Machine snapshots are not touched.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** A runner on the old version keeps leaking until it updates. A new sweep removes the old version's leftovers too, because the names are the same.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Running the sweep again removes nothing new. Running it on a missing root first creates the root through `aidevops_sensitive_temp_root`, as every headless run does now.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** A failed removal leaves the entry for the next sweep. The sweep never fails the pulse (`|| true`), as the existing pulse log cleanup does not.
- **Run time:** One directory listing per pulse worker launch, plus a walk of each candidate directory. The first run on this runner removes about 5,300 entries in a second or two. After that, a few entries per launch.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths()`, `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup()`, and the new `aidevops_sensitive_temp_sweep_stale()`
- **Current line count:** `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` 31 lines (`headless-runtime-launch.sh:134-164`); `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` 45 lines (`pulse-temp-helper.sh:57-101`); the threshold is 100
- **Estimated growth:** about +6 lines in the cleanup function, about +6 lines in the pulse cleanup, and about 60 lines for the new function with its heredoc
- **Projected post-change:** about 37, about 51 and about 60 lines, all under 100
- **Action required:** None.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh .agents/scripts/sensitive-temp-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-temp-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-sensitive-temp-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sensitive-temp-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck covers every changed file. `test-sensitive-temp-helper.sh` covers the sweep's rules. `test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh` covers the new call and its isolation. The database tests cover sidecar removal. The contract and kill-reason tests cover exit classification, which must not change.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required beyond CI's normal jobs. The change stays inside cleanup paths, and the tests above cover each one.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: the commands above
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: bound sensitive temp retention`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required; CI runs on the PR

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** Nothing in the sensitive temp root outlives the retention window, and macOS backups do not keep it, while exit classification stays the same.
- **Preserved user directions:** No repository, host or credential names in the code, commits, PR or comments.
- **Trigger and evidence:** Not triggered.
- **Completed and verified:** Nothing yet.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** All of them.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** Never run the sweep, or any test, against the runner's real `~/.aidevops-private/tmp`. Never open files in it.
- **Next safe route:** If an ordering check fails, keep the sweep (steps 2-5) and drop step 1 from this PR, noting why in the PR body.

### Scope Boundaries

Initial implementation map. Directly necessary adjacent integration follows `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery": document and verify the minimal corrected scope before editing. Explicit exclusions and hard boundaries remain binding and require a separate authorized brief-owner decision.

**Hard boundaries:**

- The sweep deletes only top-level `aidevops-*` entries of the resolved sensitive root. It never follows or removes symlinks, and never acts on any other folder.
- Pre-warmed auth folders are out of scope. They are created in the system temp folder (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1125`), not in the sensitive root, and the guardian refuses paths outside it (`sensitive-temp-helper.sh:225`).
- Leave existing Time Machine snapshots alone, and do not exclude any folder other than the temp root.
- Add no environment variable, flag, harness or CI job.

**AI brief owner:** The maintainer's interactive aidevops session that filed this issue, and otherwise Pulse terminal-blocker recovery.

**Recovery:** Preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/sensitive-temp-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_cleanup_headless_runtime_temp_paths` removes a registered path's `.wait_status`, `.kill_reason`, `.watchdog_killed`, `.watchdog_stall_killed` and `.rate_limit_fast` sidecars, and still refuses paths outside its patterns.

  ```yaml

  ```


  ```yaml
    pattern: "aidevops_sensitive_temp_sweep_stale"

  ```


  ```yaml
    method: manual
    prompt: "Review the diff and PR body for private names, paths and values."
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **A sweep as the backstop, not more guardians.** Guardians cannot survive a reboot, and every new kind of temp file would need its own registration. One age rule over the root bounds everything, whatever the cause, including the 50 guarded directories that leaked.
- **At least 24 h, derived from the guardian limit.** The guardian already expires guarded paths after 7 h even while their owner runs, so nothing in the root is meant to live that long. 24 h gives margin for sleep and clock changes. Using `max(86400, 2 * HEADLESS_RUNTIME_TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS)` keeps the sweep behind the guardian if that limit is raised.
- **Run from `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup`.** It already runs on every pulse worker launch and already sweeps stale pulse logs. That keeps the sweep off each worker's own start-up path.

## Task


Add a reusable helper that qualifies a Tailscale-compatible control plane
(Headscale, or any `--login-server`) on a Cloudron test install by starting two

server view, netcheck, peer ping and DERP status. Optionally force relay-only

## Task Brief

## What

Add a reusable helper that qualifies a Tailscale-compatible control plane
(Headscale, or any `--login-server`) on a Cloudron test install by starting two
disposable official Tailscale clients in Docker, then reporting registration,
server view, netcheck, peer ping and DERP status. Optionally force relay-only
paths.

## Why

Qualifying the Headscale Cloudron package (`marcusquinn/cloudron-headscale-app`
v0.1.0) needed an ad-hoc script to prove that real clients register with
pre-auth keys, connect directly, and connect through the embedded DERP relay.
The same proof is needed for every Headscale package update and for any
future Tailscale-compatible package. Today it would be re-invented each time.

## How

1. Create `.agents/scripts/tailscale-client-qa-helper.sh` from the reference
   implementation below. Source `shared-constants.sh`; `local var="$1"`;
   explicit `return 0/1` in every function; ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2
   compatible (macOS `/bin/bash`), so avoid empty-array expansion under
   `set -u` (the reference's `"${extra_env[@]}"` fails on Bash 3.2 when empty).
2. Subcommands: `run <app-location> [--force-derp] [--image IMAGE]`,
   `cleanup`, `help`. Make the server CLI hook explicit
   (`--server-cmd 'cloudron exec --app <app> -- headscale'` default) so
   non-Cloudron Headscale servers work too.
3. Security: never print or log the pre-auth key; create it `--ephemeral`
   with a short expiry; clear the variable after use; always remove
   containers and the `qa` user's nodes on exit (trap).
4. Exit non-zero when any client fails to reach `Running` or the peer ping
   fails; print `PASS:`/`FAIL:` lines suitable for release evidence.
5. Document it in `.agents/tools/deployment/cloudron-app-packaging.md`
   (qualification section) as the way to test Tailscale-compatible packages.

Reference implementation used for the qualification (85 lines, proven against
Headscale 0.29.5 and `tailscale/tailscale:stable`):

```bash
hs() { cloudron exec --app "$APP" -- headscale "$@"; }
key="$(hs preauthkeys create --user "$user_id" --reusable --ephemeral --expiration 30m -o json | jq -r '.key')"
docker run -d --name hs-qa-a --hostname hs-qa-a \
  -e TS_AUTHKEY="$key" -e TS_USERSPACE=true -e TS_STATE_DIR=/tmp/ts \
  -e "TS_EXTRA_ARGS=--login-server=https://$APP --hostname=hs-qa-a" \
  [-e TS_DEBUG_ALWAYS_USE_DERP=true] tailscale/tailscale:stable
hs nodes list -o json | jq -r '.[] | "\(.given_name) \(.ip_addresses | join(",")) online=\(.online)"'
docker exec hs-qa-a tailscale netcheck
docker exec hs-qa-a tailscale ping -c 5 --until-direct=false "$(docker exec hs-qa-b tailscale ip -4)"
docker exec hs-qa-a tailscale debug derp headscale
```

title: fix(pulse): runner_capability_unmet cooldown does not stop same-login redispatch of an unchanged brief (7 releases/hour on v3.39.45)
body:
## Observed

A thinking-tier award-enrichment issue in a managed private repo (placeholder: `<private-repo>#<N>`) was dispatched and released **7 times in ~60 minutes** on 2026-10-18, every time with `Terminal blocker: reason=runner_capability_unmet`, alternating across two runner logins:

| Release (UTC) | Runner | Observation revision |
|---|---|---|
| 20:07:04 | runner B | 0cab7d84… |
| 20:12:50 | runner A | c0e107a8… |
| 20:26:54 | runner B | 0cab7d84… |
| 20:34:54 | runner A | c0e107a8… |
| 20:39:41 | runner B | 0cab7d84… |
| 20:56:52 | runner A | 0fb897f0… |
| 21:05:23 | runner A | 0fb897f0… |

The last two releases are the **same login, same device (`DISPATCH_LEASE device=` identical), same observation revision**, with the redispatch lease at 21:00:13 — about 3.5 minutes after the 20:56:52 observation. All runners report `aidevops_version=3.39.45`, which includes PR #35042 (GH#35037, "cool down worker-reported capability gaps", merged 16:05Z, released in v3.39.45).

The worker checkpoint shows the underlying cause is source access (HTTP 403 `access-denied` on the publisher pages), so no runner in the current fleet may be able to satisfy it. Each attempt costs a full thinking-tier worker launch (~5 min plus ~3 min dispatch ceremony).

## Expected

After a trusted own-login `runner_capability_unmet` observation, the same login should skip the issue for `_DISPATCH_CAPABILITY_COOLDOWN_TTL_SECONDS` (default 21600s) while requirements are unchanged. When every known runner has reported the same blocker for the unchanged brief, the issue should stop cycling (fleet-wide exhaustion signal) instead of alternating across runners.

## Hypotheses (unverified — confirm before fixing)

1. **Fingerprint self-invalidation.** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:1026-1035` keys the cooldown on issue `updatedAt`. Every release/lease comment and status-label change bumps `updatedAt`, so `_dispatch_capability_cooldown_active` (line 1130) sees a mismatched fingerprint and deletes the record (line 1132). The re-import in `_dispatch_capability_cooldown_from_observation` (line 1177) should recover, so if this is the cause the re-import is also failing.
2. **Re-import does not find the observation.** `terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments` / `terminal_blocker_runner_capability_observation_epoch` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`) may reject the runner's own comments when its `author_association` on a private org repo is `CONTRIBUTOR` (same family as GH#34703), so no epoch is returned and the skip falls through.
3. **Bypass path.** The 21:00 dispatch may have come from a path that does not call `_dispatch_skip_for_capability_cooldown` (for example event-refill or the single-issue dispatcher).

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` — `_dispatch_capability_fingerprint`, `_dispatch_capability_cooldown_active`, `_dispatch_capability_cooldown_from_observation`, `_dispatch_skip_for_capability_cooldown` (lines ~1020-1215, plus the enumeration filter near line 1398)
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` — trusted-comment filtering and observation epoch
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` — existing regression pattern from PR #35042

## Verification

- Replay: own-login observation, then issue `updatedAt` bumped by a later lease/label comment, then the next candidate pass must log `runner_capability_unmet cooldown active` and not launch.
- Replay with commenter `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR` on a private repo where the commenter is the runner login.
- Optional: when observations for the unchanged revision exist from all logins in the runner set, record a single terminal decision instead of redispatching.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` pass; ShellCheck clean.

title: hostinger-helper.sh: cron list/create/delete/output via the hPanel API
body:
## What

Add `cron` subcommands to `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh` so agents manage hPanel cron jobs through the Hostinger API. Today they write a one-off script each time.

```
hostinger-helper.sh cron list   --ssh ALIAS [--json]
hostinger-helper.sh cron create --ssh ALIAS --time 'CRON' --command 'CMD' [--apply]
hostinger-helper.sh cron delete --ssh ALIAS --uid UID [--apply]
hostinger-helper.sh cron output --ssh ALIAS --uid UID
```

## Why

On Hostinger shared hosting, SSH has no `crontab`, so the hPanel API is the only way to change cron from an agent session. `services/hosting/hostinger-wordpress-cron.md` documents the API, but no helper wraps it.

In a recent session an agent concluded cron could not be changed, because `crontab -l` failed over SSH. Then it wrote a one-off script to list and create jobs. The capability should be one helper command that the cron guide names.

## How

- **Reference pattern:** `fleet_command()` in `hostinger-helper.sh`.
  - When `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` is unset, inject it with `aidevops secret HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN -- ...`, as `fleet inventory` does. Never print it.
  - `hosting_fleet.py` already reads the token from the environment, so the cron code may live there as a new subcommand if that fits better.
- **API, as observed (verify against the current docs at developers.hostinger.com before relying on it):**
  - `GET` and `POST` on `/api/hosting/v1/accounts/{username}/cron-jobs`; `POST` takes `time` and `command`.
  - `DELETE` on `/{uid}`; `GET` on `/{uid}/output`.
  - The list response is a top-level JSON array of `{uid, username, time, command}`.
  - `{username}` is the hosting account, which `ssh ALIAS whoami` returns.
- **Safety, following `hostinger-wordpress-cron.md`:**
  - `create` and `delete` preview by default and need `--apply`.
  - Before each change, write a private snapshot of the job list (mode 0600) under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/hostinger-cron/`. After it, print the list again.
  - `delete` removes only the exact UID it is given.
  - After a partial or failed response, list live jobs before any retry. Never retry blindly.
  - Mask the account home path in printed output, matching how other helpers handle private paths.
- **Docs:**
  - Add the commands to `hostinger-helper.sh help` and `services/hosting/hostinger.md`.
  - In `services/hosting/hostinger-wordpress-cron.md` ("Verify the Hostinger and runtime surface"), name the helper as the way to inspect and change jobs, and say that a missing SSH `crontab` is expected and is not a blocker.

- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger-wordpress-cron.md`

title: fix(pulse): first-observation target_code_blocker holds are never re-armed after the target code is fixed
body:
## Problem

A first terminal-blocker observation with `reason=target_code_blocker` projects `status:blocked`, but nothing ever re-arms it — not when the target code is fixed, and not on a trusted `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive. The issue stays `status:blocked` indefinitely and every downstream dependant stays blocked behind it.

Observed (private managed repo, placeholders used): a consolidated enrichment issue was blocked by a worker with `Terminal blocker: reason=target_code_blocker owner=target-maintainer`. The target-code defect was then fixed and merged (linked fix issue auto-closed `COMPLETED`). The blocked issue has zero open native blockers but remains `status:blocked`, and ~89 dependants trace to it. A point-in-time sweep of that repo found 116 `status:blocked` issues with no native blocker; terminal-blocker observations are a major contributor.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: `_TBC_REVISION_REARM_REASONS` (line ~26) excludes `target_code_blocker`, so `terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active` returns 1 ("not applicable") for it — it never models the hold at all.
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: `_tbr_seed_reason` (line ~159) only seeds (a) circuits this runner opened or (b) this runner's observations in revision-re-arm classes. A first `target_code_blocker` observation matches neither, so no runner queues it and `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` is never reached.
- Seeding is also restricted to the observing runner's own login; if that runner is offline or the observation came from another runner, no one owns recovery.
- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` intentionally preserves terminal-blocker holds (see `tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh:339`), so nothing else releases it.

The circuit's own recovery text says "Relevant revisions re-arm code/brief blockers", and `terminal_blocker_task_revision` already includes `target_revision` (default-branch HEAD) — so the intended contract is that a target-code change re-arms `target_code_blocker`. The first-observation path does not implement it.

## Proposed fix

1. Treat `target_code_blocker` as re-armable for first observations: re-arm when the computed task revision (which includes `target_revision`) differs from the observed revision, or on a trusted OWNER/MEMBER retry directive after the observation. Consider a narrower target signal (e.g. a merged PR that `Resolves` a linked blocker issue, or a change to files named in the protected dossier) if any-merge re-arming is judged too noisy — document the choice.
2. Let `_tbr_seed_candidates`/`_tbr_seed_reason` seed held observations for re-arm evaluation regardless of which runner recorded them (the release decision needs only public markers + revision; protected excerpts are only needed for the AI-owner dossier path).
3. Keep all existing exclusions in `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` (maintainer/permission/brief holds, other `status:*` labels) unchanged.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

Circuit script: re-arm semantics for `target_code_blocker` first observations. Recovery helper: seeding of other runners' held observations. Tests: target_code_blocker observation held at same revision; released after revision change; released after trusted retry; still held when other hold labels are present.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- ShellCheck clean on edited scripts.
- Live: after deploy, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh seed --force` then `pending` on a runner should release a `target_code_blocker`-held issue whose target revision has since changed and that has no other hold labels.

## Constraints

- Never release permission, maintainer-review, brief-scope or dependency holds.
- Retry directive remains scheduling-only; it grants no access (`#aidevops:trust-boundary` preserved).

## Task


Roll out the current `loc-badge.yml` caller to downstream repos whose
"Repository Metrics" workflow fails with `startup_failure` on every run, and
stop this class of breakage from recurring silently.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Roll out the current `loc-badge.yml` caller to downstream repos whose
"Repository Metrics" workflow fails with `startup_failure` on every run, and
stop this class of breakage from recurring silently.

## Why

GH#34480 (commit `50373ce840`, 2026-10-12) added job permissions
`actions: read` and `pull-requests: write` to
`.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml`. Downstream callers that use the
reusable workflow at `@main` but were installed from the older caller template
grant only a workflow-level `permissions: contents: write`. A reusable job
cannot exceed its caller's permission ceiling, so GitHub refuses to start the
run (`startup_failure`, no jobs, no logs).

Evidence (2026-10-18): `sync-workflows-helper.sh --workflow loc-badge` classifies
58 registered repos as `DRIFTED/CALLER`; the latest metrics run is
`startup_failure` in 48, `failure` in 4 and `success` in 6. Example (public):
`marcusquinn/cloudron-headscale-app`, last success 2026-10-05, startup_failure
on every push since. The current template
`.agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml` grants the job permissions
and works (for example in `marcusquinn/cloudron-opendesk-app`).

## How

1. Dry run: `sync-workflows-helper.sh --workflow loc-badge --json` and confirm
   the planned refreshes. The helper already filters out repos without
   admin/maintain access and those that are local-only, archived or external.

title: Proposal: augment security audits with independent verification, coverage ledgers, and evidence-based findings
body:
## Problem

aidevops already has useful security scanners, an external-repository audit, and a reconnaissance/source-to-sink analysis methodology. The opportunity is to strengthen the evidence and orchestration contract around those capabilities, rather than replace them or add another scanner suite.

A comparison with https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill identified several additions worth considering: independent adversarial validation, explicit finding dispositions, deterministic coverage accounting, validated structured artifacts, and current-source revalidation across runs.

**Scope of this request:** a proposal for maintainer consideration, not authorization to install an integration, change defaults, run a live audit, or dispatch a broad implementation. Third-party integration and architecture decisions remain with maintainers under `CONTRIBUTING.md`. No implementation PR is attached because the report contract, routing, and safety choices should be agreed first.

## Evidence and existing strengths

Reviewed installed aidevops **v3.39.45**, then rechecked the following upstream files on 2026-10-19. The observed upstream main commit was `fdfe2ab84c65967df214138f4f8451cf285f776d`; revalidate against the implementation base because main can advance.

| Existing surface | Observed behavior | Augmentation opportunity |
|---|---|---|
| `.agents/tools/code-review/security-audit.md:25-46,162-211` | Eleven scan categories, architecture assessment, Markdown report, category PASS/FAIL/WARN/SKIP, severity/overall-rating tables | Retain breadth while distinguishing exploitable vulnerabilities, unresolved source-grounded leads, and hardening notes |
| `.agents/tools/code-review/security-analysis.md:25-44` | Existing integrations, JSON/SARIF report documentation, two-pass reconnaissance and source-to-sink tracing | Make evidence completeness and independent verification explicit instead of relying only on the investigating agent |
| `.agents/scripts/security-helper.sh:239-320` | `cmd_analyze` selects scope, runs Secretlint when available, then directs users to the security-analysis subagent | Make scanner completion versus deep-analysis completion unambiguous; do not imply the helper already performs a multi-agent vulnerability investigation |
| `.agents/tools/security/security-audit.md:12-36` | Untrusted-source handling, no execution of target project code, secret protection, isolated clone/cleanup, delegation to the owning methodology | Preserve these boundaries and augment the existing entry point, not introduce a competing audit engine |

The audit severity table currently treats some checklist deviations as fixed-severity findings: e.g. unpinned Actions/missing Docker USER as HIGH and missing Dependabot as MEDIUM. These can be important hardening gaps, but their presence alone does not establish an exploitable trust-boundary failure or demonstrated impact.

Cloudflare reference inspected at commit `c1c8a8c1471069fb0e188eeaff69b8e8db6564a8`: `README.md`, `skills/security-audit/SKILL.md`, and `skills/security-audit/VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md`. Its relevant patterns are six-phase orchestration, fresh candidate verifiers, coverage critics, distinct verdicts, schema/ledger validators, and prior-run revalidation. This is a source review, not a benchmark of either workflow's vulnerability-discovery effectiveness.

Exact searches of the installed framework and local tracked `.agents` source found no explicit `cloudflare/security-audit-skill`/`security-audit-skill` reference or its `coverage-ledger.json`/`validate-findings.cjs` identifiers. This is limited negative evidence, not proof of no historical influence or a repository-wide provenance audit.

## Proposed Solution

### Priority 1: evidence quality and truthful completion

1. **Define explicit dispositions.** Separate `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records, with hardening advice outside confirmed vulnerability counts. Unresolved leads must identify an exact missing fact; speculative ideas are not findings. Assign vulnerability severity only to confirmed records, based on demonstrated impact and realistic preconditions. Keep hardening priority separate.
2. **Require a source-grounded evidence chain.** Record the reviewed source ref/dirty state, lower-trust principal, entrypoint, propagation, sink/boundary, source-visible preventing controls, affected resource, observed result where available, and the narrowest effective remediation. Preserve useful static findings; do not import a runtime-reproduction requirement without deciding how it fits aidevops' no-target-execution policy.
3. **Add independent adversarial validation.** A fresh bounded reviewer should attempt to refute each proposed finding against current source, rather than accept the hunter's interpretation. Reuse existing review/delegation infrastructure where suitable; review independence and output ownership must be explicit. Material upgrades to a verdict, root cause, impact, or severity need fresh verification.
4. **Distinguish stage outcomes.** Report scanner availability, scan failures, investigation completion, verification completion, and unresolved blockers separately. A successful secret scan or valid report structure is not evidence that a complete security audit ran.

### Priority 2: reproducible coverage and report artifacts

5. **Track coverage as evidence.** Add a parent-owned ledger with stable units across surfaces/trust boundaries/attack classes. Track planned, reviewed, candidate, blocked, deferred, and out-of-scope work, with source paths and reviewer/check evidence. Category status alone must not imply exhaustive coverage. A bounded gap-critic pass can identify omissions without silently expanding scope.
6. **Validate structured records, then derive prose.** Build on existing JSON/SARIF reporting rather than create a second incompatible report pipeline. Consider a versioned schema, bounded input validation, stable root-cause fingerprints, and semantic checks connecting records to coverage and evidence. Generate Markdown/SARIF from accepted records; validator success proves structure/consistency, not vulnerability truth.
7. **Revalidate across runs.** Reuse prior evidence only after checking relevant current source and conditions. Changed-source confirmations become revalidation work. Rejected claims suppress only the unchanged failed claim, not the surrounding attack surface. Never turn old blocked/deferred/unresolved work into covered work.

### Priority 3: controlled depth and progressive disclosure

8. **Make cost and scope explicit.** Consider opt-in quick/standard/deep profiles or equivalent scopes with agent budgets. Reserve verification capacity before hunting; report incomplete coverage when a budget or capability is exhausted. Keep the current quick scanner path quick and compatible.
9. **Expand domain hunting guidance selectively.** Companion documents could address tenant isolation/data lifecycle, AI tool permissions and output handling, CI/release trust, cloud/IAM, client-side messaging, RPC/queues, resource exhaustion, and native/local IPC. Load only relevant domains; reuse existing specialist docs and avoid growing always-loaded guidance.

## Safety and compatibility constraints

- Preserve read-only target inspection, no secret disclosure, no live/shared/production probing, no implicit paid API usage, and existing approval boundaries.
- The current external-audit rule forbids target-code execution. Keep that default. Sandboxed reproduction is a separate maintainer decision, not an incidental consequence of adopting this methodology.
- If reproduction is later supported, require demonstrable OS-enforced isolation: denied external networking, sanitized allowlisted environment, read-only target/toolchain, bounded scratch writes/resources/lifetime, dummy data, and safe artifact handling. Missing controls must produce an explicit blocker, never an unsandboxed fallback.
- Reuse existing bounded review roles and caller-owned artifact conventions; do not assume Cloudflare's agent names map directly to aidevops or grant researchers extra execution rights.
- Protect retained evidence from target-controlled scratch artifacts; define retention/redaction separately from clone cleanup.
- Preserve current entry points, scanner integrations, and existing report consumers. Any schema migration needs a version and compatibility plan.

## Suggested implementation surfaces and reference patterns

- Owners: `.agents/tools/code-review/security-audit.md` and `.agents/tools/code-review/security-analysis.md`.
- Entry-point alignment: `.agents/tools/security/security-audit.md`, `.agents/tools/security/security-analysis.md`, and their owning command sources. Resolve command-source/symlink layout from the current tree before editing generated copies.
- Helpers/reporting: `.agents/scripts/security-helper.sh` and existing reporting/review helpers, after inspecting their actual contracts.
- New schema, ledger validator, companion, and focused-check paths are **not selected yet**; choose the narrowest existing convention during design. No new runner, dependencies, or broad CI suite is implied.
- Reference patterns: existing source-to-sink investigation and JSON/SARIF reporting, existing independent review roles, plus the attributed Cloudflare methodology above.

## Acceptance / Verification to consider

title: runner capability: host-wide cooldown when a worker's declared secret is rejected (e.g. sign-in 401), keyed on secret names
body:
## What

When a worker's runtime credential is **rejected** (for example, an app admin sign-in returns HTTP 401), record one host-wide, runner-local marker keyed on the declared secret names. The runner should then stop claiming every issue whose `requires-secrets:` includes those names until the stored secret value changes, and it should notify the runner owner once.

## Evidence (managed private repo, 2026-10-19)

- One runner logged about 30 worker comments with "admin sign-in HTTP 401", across at least 12 different issues in a single day. Each was a fresh claim, a full source-capture session, then a stop at sign-in, and each ended `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`. The same runner published successfully on other issues in between, so the rejection may be intermittent or account-specific. Either way, every new issue re-paid the session cost.
- `runner-capability-helper.sh` gates on secret **presence** (`aidevops secret check`) and repo probes. It can't see a present but rejected value.
- `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` (around lines 1021-1033, GH#33743) keys the capability cooldown on **repo/issue** plus a requirement fingerprint. A rejection seen on issue A doesn't defer issues B…N that need the same secrets.

## How

1. Let workers declare `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REJECTED_SECRETS=NAME1,NAME2` (names only, like `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_MISSING_SECRETS` in `reference/worker-discipline.md`).
2. In the runtime release path (`headless-runtime-failure.sh` / `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`), persist a runner-local record of those names, the time, and a hash of each secret's current stored value. Never store or print the values themselves.
3. In `runner-capability-helper.sh`, defer any candidate whose requirements include a recorded name while the stored-value hash is unchanged. Re-arm automatically when the value changes or after a bounded TTL (default 24 hours), so intermittent failures recover.
4. Post one owner-facing notice per marker, through the existing runner health or notification path, not per issue: "secret NAME rejected on runner R; refresh it with `aidevops secret set NAME`".

## Verification

Extend `tests/test-runner-capability.sh` with four cases:
- A recorded rejection defers a different issue that requires the same name.
- Changing the stored value re-arms it.
- An issue that needs only unrelated secrets is still admitted.
- No secret value appears in output.
